raw_suggestions.name: nutrient deficiency
raw_suggestions.description: Nutrient deficiency is caused by a lack of macronutrients or micronutrients essential for the plant. This can be caused by insufficient amounts of nutrients in the soil or unsuitable conditions for nutrients uptake.
raw_suggestions.treatment: Replant the plant into fresh soil rich in nutrients.; Add manure or compost to the soil.; Apply missing nutrients to the plant foliage (suitable for quick help). Follow the instructions on the chosen product to prevent excessive fertilizer usage.; Apply missing nutrients to the soil (suitable for long-term help). Follow the instructions on the chosen product to prevent excessive fertilizer usage.; Apply fertilizer regularly. Fertilizing is especially important during spring and summer.; Change the soil regularly. Plants should be repotted when the soil is compacted, depleted of nutrients, and no longer retains water.

raw_suggestions.name: Xylella fastidiosa
raw_suggestions.description: Xylella fastidiosa is a harmful bacterium that lives in a plant’s xylem (the tubes that move water). It clogs these tubes, so parts of the plant dry out even when the soil is moist. Typical signs include brown, crispy leaf edges (leaf scorch), yellowing between veins, stunted growth, one-sided dieback on shoots or branches, early leaf drop, and small or shrivelled fruit. It spreads mainly by small sap-feeding insects such as spittlebugs and sharpshooters, and by moving infected plants or cuttings. Many plants can be affected, including olive, grapevine, citrus, almond, cherry, lavender, rosemary, oleander, oak, and maple. This is a regulated disease in many regions.
raw_suggestions.treatment: Remove and securely dispose of badly affected plants by sealing them in bags and binning them, and do not compost them.; Prune out dead or declining branches in dry weather and disinfect tools between cuts with 70 percent alcohol.; Where permitted, reduce insect vectors by using horticultural oil or insecticidal soap targeted at nymphs on nearby weeds and groundcover.; Apply kaolin clay sprays to create a protective film that discourages feeding on some crops.; Buy plants from reputable, certified suppliers.; Isolate new plants for a few weeks and watch for symptoms before placing them near established plants.

raw_suggestions.name: Fungi
raw_suggestions.description: Fungi take energy from the plants on which they live, causing damage to the plant. Fungal infections are responsible for approximately two-thirds of infectious plant diseases and cause wilting, molding, rusts, scabs, rotted tissue, and other problems.
raw_suggestions.treatment: If possible remove and destroy the infected parts of the plant. Burn it, toss it into the garbage, or bury it deeply. Do not compost.; Apply ecological products for plant protection (e.g. neem oil, baking soda, soap).; If necessary, apply a fungicide. If you don' know the fungus species, choose fungicide based on the infected plant (e.g. house plant, garden plant, tree).; Use resistant species and cultivars as well as healthy, certified seeds and seedlings.; Ensure having good soil drainage to avoid overwatering.
